principles: Resolve gitCwd ONCE at a single choke-point boundary, not scattered re-resolution per git call (single source of truth for the resolution).
Fall back to root when no gitRoot resolves so plain repos are byte-identical (zero behavior change for the common case is the safety floor).
The contract must FAIL on the actual defect shape it claims to guard — a green contract over a live defect is worse than no contract (close the blind spots, do not just add sites).
Stay within the confirmed wrapper-root blast radius; explicitly LOG deferred backtick sites rather than silently leave the contract red or balloon scope.
drivers: A wrapper-root project (metadataRoot != gitRoot) is currently HARD-BLOCKED from DONE — the highest-severity, operator-facing symptom.
The defect recurred precisely because the B-db56 contract could be silenced by a trivial alias; without closing both blind spots it recurs a 4th time.
B-99b6 will wire this contract into the validate gate; it must be green at DONE or it blocks B-99b6.
NORMAL channel + gate/guard riskSignal: changes touch DONE-gate and authority-receipt semantics — high blast radius if wrong.

options.name: A-thread-and-strengthen
pros: Reuses the existing resolveGitCwd choke-point (transition-orchestrator already resolves doneGitCwd at :271).
Byte-identical for plain repos via root fallback.
Closes the recurrence path (alias + backtick detection) without a full rewrite.
Bounded blast radius: fix confirmed wrapper-root sites, log the rest.
cons: Must carefully not leave the contract red if many backtick sites flagged.

options.name: B-done-oracle-only
cons: Defect class recurs (the whole point is the contract was silenced); rejected by background.

options.name: C-single-helper-rewrite
pros: Ideal end-state; structurally impossible to bypass.
cons: Far too large for one story (~14+ backtick sites + all literal sites); high regression risk; rejected as out of scope.

rationale: Approach A reuses the real choke-point resolveGitCwd, keeps plain repos byte-identical via root fallback, fixes the confirmed wrapper-root false-block (done-oracle) and undefined-hash (evidence-freshness) defects, and closes BOTH contract blind spots (alias + backtick) so the class cannot recur — while bounding scope by fixing confirmed bare-root sites and logging any oversized backtick blast radius as a documented follow-up. B (only fix done-oracle, leave contract gameable) is rejected (recurrence). C (full shared-helper rewrite) is rejected (too large for one story).

preMortem.scenario: The done-oracle git-status fix changes behavior for plain (non-wrapper) repos
preMortem.trigger: resolveGitCwd returns something other than root in a plain repo, or the fallback is not wired so a null/undefined cwd is passed
preMortem.consequence: DONE gate breaks for the common case (every normal story), a far worse regression than the wrapper-root edge case
preMortem.mitigation: Explicit fallback to root when resolveGitCwd does not resolve a distinct gitRoot; add a plain-repo regression asserting the git-working-tree row is byte-identical before/after; resolveGitCwd already falls back to projectRoot by contract.

preMortem.scenario: The strengthened contract flags far more backtick sites than this story can safely fix, and the implementer leaves it RED to ship
preMortem.trigger: backtick scan flags ~14 sites; fixing all threads gitCwd through many unrelated handlers; time/scope pressure
preMortem.consequence: DONE with a red contract blocks B-99b6 (which wires it into the gate) and re-opens the very gap this story closes
preMortem.mitigation: Bounded policy: fix the CONFIRMED wrapper-root bare-root sites (done path, authority-receipt, the 4 INIT-measured sites if reachable) + ship the alias-detection rule; for any oversized remainder, add them to a documented allowlist with a scoped follow-up note so the contract stays GREEN; verify exit 0 explicitly before TEST.

preMortem.scenario: The alias-detection regex is too broad and false-positives on legitimate non-git aliases
preMortem.trigger: a const x = projectRoot that is NOT used as a git cwd gets flagged
preMortem.consequence: contract goes red on innocent code; either the implementer weakens the rule back to uselessness or churns unrelated files
preMortem.mitigation: Scope the alias detection to aliases that are subsequently used as a cwd in a git call window (same proximity model as the existing GIT_CALL_REGEX window); add KNOWN-GOOD self-test fixtures (alias not used as git cwd = 0 violations) AND KNOWN-BAD (alias used as git cwd without resolveGitCwd = 1 violation) so the rule is pinned both ways.

preMortem.scenario: Resolving gitCwd inside the DONE merge path interacts badly with the main-write-lock / autoSync already using doneGitCwd
preMortem.trigger: double resolution or a different resolved value between :271 (autoSync) and the gate call leads to divergent cwd for divergence-check vs status-check
preMortem.consequence: DONE gate and autoSync operate on different working trees → inconsistent dirty/divergence verdicts
preMortem.mitigation: Pass the SAME doneGitCwd already resolved at :271 into runDonePreMergeGate (do not re-resolve); single resolution point feeds both autoSync and the oracle gate.
